title: The analysis tree: fill each cell once
outcomes: Lays out a table of candidates, replies and one-word verdicts for a forcing position
Judges a candidate by its worst cell, not its best
Knows two ways a tree fails: a missing reply and going back over a branch
Recognises a quiet position where a tree has no verdicts to find

steps.text: A **tree** is a table you fill once. Rows are your candidates. For each, write the opponent's best replies (two is a start) and follow every branch about four plies to its end. At the end write **one word**: *mates, wins, even* or *loses* (judge by material). Fill each cell once, in order, and do not jump back. A candidate is only as good as its worst cell for you.

steps.caption: White to move. Three candidates, each followed against the best defence. A) Rh1+ : every reply loses to mate, so its cell says mates. B) Nxf7+ : White ends at least two points down, so loses. C) Rg4 : no net material change, so even. The best row is A.

line.say: Rh1+ gives check, and the king on h8 has no legal move of its own.
Black can only interpose the rook on h6.
Rxh6 is checkmate: the g3 rook covers g7 and g8, the h6 rook covers h7.

claims.statement: Rh1+ forces checkmate within two moves, whatever Black replies (depth 16).
After Rh1+ the king on h8 has no legal move.
The rook on g3 attacks g7 and g8.
After Rxh6 the rook on h6 attacks h7.
After Nxf7+ and Black's best defence White ends at least 2 points down.
Nxf7+ is at least 3 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
After Rg4 and the best defence White's net material change is zero.
Rg4 is at least a pawn worse than the best move (depth 16).

steps.text: **When a tree works.** It works when branches end in a clear verdict within about four plies: checks, captures, threats. It fails in two ways. A reply you never listed (the table looks complete and is not), and going back over a branch you already judged. In a quiet position branches never end, and a tree is the wrong tool. Four plies and two replies are rules of thumb.

steps.title: Same candidate, one extra defender
steps.prompt: In the first position A) Ra7+ mates. In the second a black knight stands on c8; everything else is the same. Fill the cell for Ra7+ before you answer: which reply did the first table not have?

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** Each exercise has three hints. The next three are silent and share one position: three candidates. Fill your table on paper first, then answer. The plan is to offer hints only on request once you solve unlabeled items without them (planned, not built yet).

steps.prompt: Look at your paper table for the silent position. Count honestly. This note stays on this device.

steps.text: **Tree sheet: ten minutes, away from the app.** Draw three rows and two columns. Rows are your candidates; columns are the opponent's two best replies. Follow each branch four plies and write one verdict word per cell. Tick each finished cell; put a dot each time you go back to one. Then check the best row against an engine or a book. Fewer dots is the aim.
